tagline: From Lake Pend Oreille up the gold rush trail to Canada.
intro: The byway starts downtown in Sandpoint, on the shore of Lake Pend Oreille, and runs north on US 95 through the McArthur Lake Wildlife Corridor to Bonners Ferry on the Kootenai River. Beyond town, Idaho 1 turns off east of Copeland and goes north about 11 miles to the Canadian line at Porthill.

It follows the Wild Horse Trail, which mattered to the Kootenai Tribe and later to the settlers of the gold rush years. When gold turned up in the East Kootenays of British Columbia in 1863, thousands of prospectors went north this way, and a Walla Walla merchant named Edwin Bonner set up a ferry where the trail crossed the Kootenai.

moments.title: McArthur Lake Wildlife Corridor
moments.text: Grizzly bears moving between the Selkirk and Cabinet mountains pass through this corridor, and the highway across it has a high rate of collisions with wildlife.

moments.title: Bonners Ferry
moments.text: The town once stood on stilts against the spring floods, until brick buildings replaced them and the drained valley below became known as the Nile of the North.

moments.title: Porthill
moments.text: Before it took the name of Charles Plummer Hill, its customs officer and postmaster, the settlement at the border was Ockonook, meaning a grassy hillside with rocks.
